newsitem.title: USA: John Kennedy Jr. writes about his errant cousins.
newsitem.headline: John Kennedy Jr. writes about his errant cousins.

text.p: John F. Kennedy Jr. tackles the controversies surrounding his cousins Joseph and Michael Kennedy in the new issue of his monthly political magazine George, saying they became "poster boys for bad behaviour."

Writing about temptation in the editor's letter in the September issue of George, Kennedy said the two men had "chased an idealised alternative to their life" and "perhaps ... should have known better."
His words were unusual in that Kennedy family members rarely speak out publicly about one another, especially in scandals and other controversies.
John F. Kennedy Jr. is the only son of the late U.S. president, and Joseph and Michael Kennedy are sons of the president's late brother, U.S. Attorney General Robert Kennedy.

Joseph Kennedy, a Democratic member of the U.S. House of Representatives from Massachusetts, had his 12-year marriage to Sheila Rauch Kennedy annulled last year, three years after he remarried. The annulment prompted his first wife to write a book titled "Shattered Faith" opposing that Roman Catholic process.
Joseph's younger brother Michael allegedly had a five-year affair with a teenage babysitter, but authorities did not file charges because the alleged victim would not cooperate.

For an issue listing "the 20 most fascinating women in politics," John Kennedy Jr. commented on the view that leading a respectable life leads to temptation, but conformity produces a suffocating life.

"I've seen the cycle up close in the past year," he wrote. "Two members of my family chased an idealised alternative to their life. One left behind an embittered wife, and another, in what looked to be a hedge against mortality, fell in love with youth and surrendered his judgment in the process. Both became poster boys for bad behaviour.

"Perhaps they deserved it. Perhaps they should have known better. To whom much is given, much is expected, right? The interesting thing was the ferocious condemnation of their excursions beyond the bounds of acceptable behaviour. Since when does someone need to apologise on television for getting divorced?

"But perhaps there was some comfort in watching the necessary order assert itself. The discontents of civilised life look positively benign when compared with the holy terror visited upon the brave and stupid."

The essay was accompanied by a picture of Kennedy, seemingly nude, with just his heavily muscled arms and legs emerging from dark shadow. The cover of the magazine featured a nude photograph of model Kate Moss, posing as Eve in the garden of Eden.
Joseph Kennedy, speaking to reporters in Chelsea, Massachusetts, said he had not read the essay.

"I guess my first reaction was 'Ask not what you can do for your cousin but what you can do for his magazine,'" he said -- a reference to President Kennedy's famous 1961 injunction in his inaugural address, "And so, my fellow Americans, ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country."
The congressman added, "I think this is just the sort of normal give-and-take of politics."
"John has got his own life and his own way of articulating his particular views on issues," Kennedy said. "He's my cousin, he's my friend, and that's the end of it."
Joseph Kennedy is expected to run for governor of Massachusetts next year. Opinion polls show his popularity has dropped over the issue of his annulment.
